subject: Cloud vendor gap analysis + SDK migration test plan
messages:
From: Patrick Lowe <plowe@finlytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T16:12:00-05:00
Subject: Quick follow-up: Redwood demo & migration questions

Thanks for the demo earlier today — Elena and I appreciated the focused run-through of latency profiles and the Dedicated options. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we scope an initial migration POC: 

- We need clarity on OpenAI-compatible endpoints: request/response shapes, streaming semantics, and function-calling parity.
- Tokenization differences: are there known differences vs OpenAI that could change prompt engineering or cost?
- Hyperscaler comparison: we ran a quick set on AWS Bedrock and saw higher p95 latency for long contexts. Would like to see a side-by-side on our 1k prompt set.
- Security/compliance: we have a short SOC2 checklist — can your team confirm what artifacts you can share for a procurement review?

Elena attached our current architecture diagram (current_arch_diagram.png) — that should help you see where inference would sit in our stack.

Can we lock a plan for the next two weeks to run the compatibility and perf tests? Proposed window: Nov 22–29.

Thanks,
Patrick
Patrick Lowe
Head of Platform Engineering, Finlytics
plowe@finlytics.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Patrick Lowe <plowe@finlytics.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@finlytics.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: Redwood demo & migration questions

Patrick — thanks for the clear notes and the diagram. Replied inline below and sketched a lightweight test plan we can run during Nov 22–29. I've attached a short test plan (redwood_test_plan_v1.md). High level: we will validate API compatibility, tokenization diffs, and run a perf matrix vs both Bedrock and a public OpenAI endpoint.

Quick answers:
- OpenAI-compatible endpoints: we support an OpenAI-style REST surface (chat completion, streaming, function calling) with some extra headers for routing/quantization control. Response payloads follow the same shape (choices, usage) but we include an additional X-Redwood-Model header for runtime metadata. We'll share a compatibility spec by EOD Monday.
- Tokenization: there are small tokenization differences for a few legacy tokenizers; on most modern models differences are negligible, but we'll run a token-diff report on your 1k prompt set.
- Hyperscaler perf: agree — long-context p95s diverge. We'll run: Bedrock baseline, OpenAI baseline (if you can provide keys/test access), and Redwood hosted + dedicated config.
- Compliance artifacts: Grace will coordinate SOC2/pen-test artifacts and redact where necessary.

Proposed test plan (summary):
1) API parity smoke: run 20 canonical prompts covering chat, streaming, function calls.
2) Tokenization diff: token counts + tokenization map for 1k prompt set.
3) Perf matrix: small/medium/long contexts (sequence lengths 64/512/2048) across Bedrock, OpenAI, Redwood-hosted (and Dedicated if you want to include later). Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens.
4) Quality spot-check: 50 prompt pairs to look for hallucination/regression.

Deliverables & Owners:
- Redwood: compatibility spec (Sean), token-diff report (Ben), perf run and spreadsheet (Ben), SOC2 artifacts & redaction note (Grace).
- Finlytics: access to evaluation keys/endpoints (Patrick), prioritized prompt set & expected outputs (Elena).

Next steps:
- Can you share test keys and the 1k prompt set by EOD Friday (Nov 19)?
- Ben and I will begin infrastructure prep and coordinate a Monday kickoff (Nov 22).

Attachments: redwood_test_plan_v1.md

—
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0122

From: Patrick Lowe <plowe@finlytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T11:18:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up: Redwood demo & migration questions

Thanks Sean — we can get the prompt set and a short tokenization reference file to you by EOD. We will also spin up a Bedrock test key and provide temporary OpenAI test credentials (limited quota) so you can run the head-to-head.

One more ask: our legal team will want an overview of fallback policies and SLA behaviors if we route from our app to a Dedicated pool vs hosted. Any doc you can point them to would help accelerate procurement.

Patrick

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-20T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Finlytics POC — owners & immediate asks

Grace / Ben — looping you both in to own the two parallel tracks: compliance artifacts and perf compatibility. High level plan and asks below. Keeping external thread intact so Finlytics sees progress.

Ask list:
- Grace: please pull SOC2 sysdescription, last pen-test executive summary, and a brief note on data retention/keys (KMS options). Redact anything customer-specific; Patrick will handle NDA-specific asks.
- Ben: run tokenization diff and perf harness. Priority for Nov 22 kickoff: prep containerized runner we can point at three endpoints (Bedrock, OpenAI test keys, Redwood-hosted). Output should be a single CSV with per-prompt token counts and latency metrics.
- Both: document the API parity gaps (if any) per function-call, streaming, and choice semantics. If small diffs exist, propose short mitigation notes.

Timeline: prep by Nov 21 so we can kickoff Nov 22. We should have a mid-run sync on Nov 24 and final summary by Nov 29.

Sean

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Finlytics POC — owners & immediate asks

Quick status update: infra & runner ready. Benchmarks plan attached (benchmarks_plan.csv). Initial notes after a 100-prompt dry run against Bedrock and Redwood-hosted:

- Tokenization: average token count delta is +0.7 tokens per prompt on our tokenizer vs OpenAI reference for the sample. Not material, but we'll include per-prompt diffs.
- Function-calling parity: payload shapes identical in 95% of cases; difference arises when streaming + function call interleaving occurs — Redwood currently sends final function call payload in the final chunk (we'll document).
- Perf: p95 on long contexts (2048) is ~22% lower on Redwood-hosted vs Bedrock in this dry run; full matrix pending.

Next: full 1k run starts today. I will upload results to the shared drive and post the summary to HubSpot when complete.

Ben
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
